title: Qualia the Purple
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Junior high student Marii Yukari sees every person as a robot through her purple eyes, an ability that helps police but isolates her; her one friend is Hatou 'Gaku' Manabu. When Yukari is drawn into a secret organization, Manabu enters a world of quantum experiments and alternate universes, trying across countless timelines to save her. Adapted by Shirou Tsunashima from Hisamitsu Ueo's light novel; three volumes, published by Seven Seas.
life_message: Love for one person can justify any effort across every possible world, though what that devotion costs is left unsettling.

content.note: Serial killer plot and murders (MU Serial Killer, Murder; AniList Gore minor); reviewer calls it unpleasant but restrained.
Psychological thriller, repeated deaths across timelines (AniList Tragedy, Time Manipulation; Okazu).
Subdued yuri crush; Okazu reports an explicit alternate-timeline relationship between Manabu and the much younger Alice (to verify); MangaDex rates it safe.
Obsessive love; reviewer says Manabu becomes 'a monster' in pursuit of her goal (Okazu; AniList Yandere, MU Obsessive Love).

Dignity vs honor.evidence: No honor culture; worth tied to Yukari's inherent value to Manabu.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Manabu defies the secret institute and physical law alike (Okazu).

Civic vs kin.evidence: One beloved friend outweighs everyone else in every world.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Institute authority opposed rather than deferred to.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Copenhagen interpretation and wave-function collapse drive the plot (Okazu).

folkways.japan: Uses the Japanese light-novel 'sekai-kei' pattern, where one schoolgirl bond decides the fate of worlds.

delivery.evidence: Okazu: heavily narrated by Manabu, who addresses the reader; long physics exposition rather than visual storytelling.
delivery.note: Ideas are explained at length in narration, but the story questions rather than endorses Manabu's choices.

winners_losers: Manabu reaches her goal at great moral cost; Yukari is reduced to the object of that goal; sympathy is split.
